title: The Conclave Process
summary: We introduce a stochastic model for the papal conclave in which $n$ cardinals vote repeatedly among themselves until one cardinal receives all the votes. In each round, the probability that a cardinal votes for a given candidate is proportional to the $α$-th power of that candidate's vote count in the preceding round. For $α=1$, the model reduces to the Wright-Fisher model and is dual to Kingman's n-coalescent. We reveal a sharp transition in the absorption time $\mathcal{T}$ at $α=1$.
